status: normative candidate; behavior qualification is recorded separately
foreign_abi: (const u8 *source, u64 source_len, u8 *output, u64 output_capacity, u8 *workspace, u64 workspace_len) -> u64; f0 returns u32 zero-extended

precedence: If source_len<64 or output_capacity<64 return SHORT before reading any source bytes.
Otherwise reject source_len!=64 or workspace_len!=0 as INVALID.
Reject revision!=1, nonzero reserved words, entry outside0..1, phase outside0..8, event outside0..9 as INVALID.
Reject every entry/phase/event triple absent from the exact transition table as INVALID.
After all validation, write exactly output[0:64] and return OK.
transport.no_write_on_nonzero: No output or workspace byte changes; source is always unchanged. Output tail beyond64 is unchanged on success.
transport.semantic_errors: Parse, effects and writer errors are facts carried by callbacks; every listed transition returns C status0 including failure terminals. No ABI error stands in for semantic rollback.
transport.pointer_preconditions: Caller supplies live memory for each nonempty advertised range; source/output are disjoint. Workspace length is zero and pointer may be null. Native retains no pointer.
transport.stateless_scope: Each call is a pure transition. Replaying an identical valid request is deterministic and allowed; no process-global history or anti-replay claim. The Rust adapter exclusively owns its continuation and executes each requested action once. A terminal phase has no valid event.

native_owns: writer error precedence over parse/effects error
empty versus committed delta terminal selection
rust_owns: original typed values and error object ownership
execution of the existing parser and native effects/summary components
identical original writeln! expressions and async effects await
validation and materialization of the native-selected terminal Rust value
error_rules: Parse diagnostic failure returns the writer io::Error and empty exact delta. Successful diagnostic returns the original ParseError and empty exact delta.
Successful effects call summary. Summary failure returns its writer io::Error and a clone of the committed delta, with no stderr diagnostic.
Effects failure computes its to_string() once and writes stderr before downcasting. A failed diagnostic returns the writer io::Error and a clone of committed delta.
After successful effects diagnostic, From<&io::Error> reconstructs kind+to_string with context I/O error; non-io keeps context=msg and source=io::Error::other(original anyhow error).
On success or preserved effects failure the committed delta is moved exactly as before. No operation is replayed or rolled back.
semantic_boundary.async: The existing effects future is awaited exactly once in its original order. Native calls are synchronous; no new yield/cancellation point is introduced. Cancellation while the host future is pending does not issue a resume or replay.
semantic_boundary.public_signatures: Unchanged. apply_patch/apply_hunks default wrappers remain source-identical and route through the native with-options functions under hia-native. Default options are NormalizeToLf and follow_symlinks=true; no implicit environment read.
semantic_boundary.source_routing: Only a new cfg module and imports plus three exact cfg guards; whole lib.rs can be inverted byte-for-byte to the clean baseline and then by the existing inverse to the complete original.
